reason: I've had a dry cough for a week and want a COVID test.
diagnosis: ACE-inhibitor–induced dry cough from recently started ramipril, suggested by the cough beginning shortly after starting the medication and the absence of infectious or cardiopulmonary symptoms.
keyPoints: Onset and timing of cough relative to starting ramipril
Character of cough: dry, persistent, no sputum or blood
Screen for COVID/infectious symptoms: fever, sore throat, loss of smell/taste, sick contacts, travel
Cardiorespiratory red flags: shortness of breath, wheeze, chest pain, palpitations, hemoptysis, edema, syncope
Medication history including recent ACE inhibitor use and other drugs
Smoking, vaping, marijuana, and environmental irritants/exposures
Past history of similar cough and chronic conditions like diabetes
manner: anxious, health-conscious, a bit repetitive, reassured
transcript:

P: Hi. Uh, I've just had this cough for the past week and I was worried I might have Covid so I just wanted to um I just wanted to be checked.
D: Sure, so you mentioned you, it started a week ago.
P: Yeah.
D: Has it been persistent or does it come and go?
P: Um it's just been there.
D: Been there. OK.
P: Yeah, I just get this itchy sort of uh like scratchy sensation in my throat. And then I just cough and um that makes it better.
D: OK. OK, uhm what, how would you describe your cough like is it barky? Is it harsh? Is it muffled?
P: Uhm no, I don't I don't think it's barky or harsh.
D: OK, and does anything make it better or worse like you know, like the cold air, laying down, at particular time of day?
P: Not really, I haven't uh, nothing's really helped. Um I also tried a cough syrup, um it didn't, it helped for a couple hours, but then it was back again. The cough was back again.
D: OK, and have you ever experienced anything like this in the past?
P: Uh well, I I said yeah when I get a cold.
D: Mhmm, OK.
P: Once a year maybe.
D: Once a year? OK. Um do you experience any shortness of breath with this cough?
P: No.
D: No, OK. Is it a dry cough or do you bring up any phlegm?
P: No, it's a dry cough.
D: OK, uh any blood that you've seen?
P: No, no.
D: No, OK. And do you feel wheezy?
P: No.
D: No, chest pain?
P: No.
D: No, um feeling like your heart's racing?
P: No.
D: Any swelling in your limbs?
P: Uh no.
D: No, any fainting spells?
P: Uhm, no.
D: No, OK. Do you ever feel like your nose is stuffy or runny?
P: No.
D: No, any changes in your vision or hearing?
P: Uh no.
D: A sore throat?
P: No.
D: Um loss of smell or taste?
P: No.
D: Any weight loss?
P: Uh no.
D: Fevers?
P: I checked no, no, I don't have a fever.
D: No, any rashes?
P: No.
D: Issues uh, any changes in your bowel movements?
P: Um uh no, I've just been constipated from time to time, but that's nothing, that's not new.
D: OK, constipation. And I'm sorry when did your constipation start?
P: Oh it's a problem for years. I don't eat enough fibre.
D: Oh, OK. Any changes in your urine?
P: No.
D: OK, any nausea or vomiting?
P: Uh, no.
D: No, OK. Any joint pain?
P: No.
D: No, numbness or tingling?
P: No.
D: Headaches?
P: No.
D: No, OK. Are you otherwise healthy? Do you have any longstanding medical conditions?
P: I have diabetes.
D: OK, how long have you had diabetes?
P: It's about, it's been uh seven years now.
D: OK, any hospitalizations or surgeries in the past?
P: No.
D: OK and um how about medications? Are you on any?
P: Uh yeah, I've been taking uh metformin for the past uh, for the past five years, when, five or six years.
D: OK.
P: Um and uh my family Doc started me on uh ramipril about two weeks ago, he told me that uh now that I'm 50, I need to I need to be on this pill as well, so now I have to take 2 pills instead of one.
D: OK.
P: Yeah because I think it's it's good for my heart or something.
D: Yeah, for sure. So you started that two weeks ago, OK. Are you up to date with all your immunizations?
P: Uh yeah, I think so.
D: OK, any allergies?
P: Uhm penicillin, I just get uh I get a rash. I got a rash when I was a child, I haven't had it since then.
D: OK, OK. Any family history of lung or heart conditions?
P: Uh no, nothing like that.
D: No, OK. Do you smoke?
P: Uh, no.
D: No, how about, uh, marijuana or other recreational drugs?
P: No.
D: No, OK, um alcohol?
P: Uh yeah, I drink on the weekends.
D: OK, what do you drink and how much do you drink?
P: I'll have maybe two or three uh bottles of beer.
D: OK sure, and um have you been in contact with any sick people recently?
P: No, no, I've just been staying at home.I'm just scared of covid, but I'm I'm still worried I might have somehow gotten it.
D: Yeah, for sure. Uhm, any travel recently?
P: No.
D: No, OK. And where do you live right now?
P: I live in a house with my wife and my two kids.
D: OK, uh are they healthy?
P: Yeah, they're all healthy.
D: OK. Any old carpet, dust, mold, or asbestos in your home?
P: Um not that I'm aware of.
